question: im a freshman and kinda lost. whats the difference between a major, gen eds, and electives? do they all count toward the 128 credits
answer:
Your undergraduate degree consists of General Education, a major, and free electives; you may also pursue a minor or second major. The pages identify these as separate parts but don’t explain the detailed meaning of “major” or “free electives.” [2]

Gen Ed is a set of ten courses: four keystone courses, one course in each of four keystone categories, and one course in two of three distribution categories. [3] A Fall 2026 page lists the distribution categories as Culture and Creativity, Values and Ethics, and Social Systems and Society; it says the “out of school requirement” is no longer enforced in degree audit tools. [5]

They are all parts of the undergraduate degree, but the pages don’t explicitly confirm how every course in each part applies to the 128-credit total. Ramapo requires 128 credits overall, and program credit requirements differ; review your classes and credits with your adviser. [2][6]

The Center for Student Success advises first-year students. Contact it at success@ramapo.edu or (201) 684-7441. [9]

question: do I have to declare a major right away or can I stay undecided for a bit
answer:
You can stay undeclared for a while, but not indefinitely. Ramapo says undergraduate students pursuing a bachelor’s degree must declare in their sophomore year before completing 64 credits [7]; matriculated students must declare by 64 credits toward graduation [10]. After completing 64 credits, you are considered a junior and must have declared [2]. For an undeclared student with at least 48 but fewer than 64 credits who is enrolled for a subsequent term, the college gives notice to declare before registering for more than 64 credits; a registration hold prevents registration if you try to register for 64 or more credits without a major. Submit the online Major/Minor Declaration form to the Registrar; upon receipt, it removes the hold and you can register [10].

If you intend to graduate in four years, aim to declare during sophomore year. Most majors take at least two years to complete and usually have foundation classes you can take in your first year; some sequential science majors should be started right away. Recommended Graduation Plans can help plan your first semester [3].

Undeclared students are advised through the Ramapo Exploration Program (REP) by academic advisors in the Center for Student Success [6]. Contact the Center for Student Success for advisement: (201) 684-7441 or success@ramapo.edu [5]. As an undeclared student, select “No Changes” if you do not wish to declare now [8].

question: what are the gen ed requirements at ramapo? like how many classes in each category
answer:
Ramapo students take 10 General Education courses: [12]
- 4 keystone courses: First Year Seminar, Social Science Inquiry, Critical Reading & Writing 102 (within the first 64 credits), and Studies in the Arts & Humanities. [12]
- 1 course in each of 4 keystone categories: Global Awareness, Historical Perspectives, Scientific Reasoning, and Quantitative Reasoning (within the first 64 credits). [12]
- 1 course in 2 of 3 distribution categories: Culture & Creativity; Systems, Sustainability, & Society; and Values & Ethics. At least one distribution course must be offered by a school other than the one housing your major. [12]
The Provost page says that starting Fall 2026 the “out of school requirement” is no longer enforced in degree audit tools; it names the third category “Social Systems and Society,” unlike section 12. The pages differ on enforcement and category wording. [11][12]
Students transferring with at least 48 credits (and returning students with at least 48 Ramapo credits at re-enrollment) have some requirements waived, but still must take Critical Reading and Writing 102, Quantitative Reasoning, Scientific Reasoning, and one course from each of two distribution categories at Ramapo. Advisement identifies what remains. [9]
Approved Gen Ed courses: https://catalog.ramapo.edu/college-wide-programs/gened#general-education-categories-and-courses [10]. Curriculum map: https://www.ramapo.edu/provost/wp-content/uploads/sites/380/2023/06/General-Education-Curriculum-Map-2019-2020.pdf [12]

question: Is there a major in nursing, and what do I need to take my first year to get in?
answer:
Yes. Ramapo offers the Nursing Generic BSN, a Bachelor of Science in Nursing [2]. Nursing MSN is also listed [2].

For the generic track, the 2026–2027 recommended plan is [2]:
• First Year, Fall Semester (total 17 credits): INTD 101 - FIRST YEAR SEMINAR (4); CHEM 111 - PRINCIPLES OF CHEMISTRY LECTURE (4); CHEM 111L - PRINCIPLES OF CHEM LAB/RECITAT (1); CRWT 102 - CRITICAL READING AND WRITING II (4); General Education Requirement * (4); PATH 001 - CAREER PATHWAYS MOD 1.
• First Year, Spring Semester (total 16 credits): General Education Requirement * (4) twice; PSYC 101 - INTRODUCTION TO PSYCHOLOGY (4); Quantitative Reasoning – MATH 108 - ELEMENTARY PROBABILITY AND STATISTICS (4).

The plan says students complete general education and science requirements in the first two years; upon satisfactory completion, they enter the two-year nursing sequence [2]. Pre-Nursing requires all listed science courses (BIOL 212/212L, BIOL 214/214L, BIOL 216/216L, CHEM 111/111L, and PSYC 101) and one math course: MATH 108 or PSYC 242 [2]. The plan schedules some of these after first year [2].

Plan: https://www.ramapo.edu/recommended-graduation-plan-2026/tas/nursing/ [2]

Sources: [2](https://catalog.ramapo.edu/programs/SN-BSN-NURG)

question: Can you tell me what the Critical Reading and Writing course is and whether everyone has to take it?
answer:
CRWT 101, Critical Reading and Writing I, is a 4-credit course that develops critical reading and writing skills, including analyzing texts, rhetorical strategies, MLA formatting, information literacy, and revision. It is writing intensive. [3] CRWT 101S covers the same material and includes one additional weekly class meeting for support. [4][6]

Not everyone takes CRWT 101: it is the first course in the progression, and placement determines where students begin. [6][7][9] CRWT 101 requires CRWT 080 or CRWT 090, or qualifying ACCUPLACER scores. [3] Students placed into developmental courses should plan to register for and complete them before or during their first semester. [10]

All Ramapo students must complete Critical Reading and Writing II (CRWT 102) as a General Education keystone course; CRWT 102 must be taken within the first 64 credits. [14][15] Students with an SAT Evidence-Based Reading & Writing score of 620 or higher are placed in CRWT 102. [8] Ramapo requires entering students to take the Reading/Essay Placement Test to determine appropriate course placement. [7]

question: whats the suggested 4 year plan for business admin majors
answer:
The catalog lists Management BS, not a “Business Administration” major. Here is the Management plan; it applies to students admitted to the major in 2026–2027. [2][3]

**Management BS — Fall 2026 recommended plan** [2]
- Year 1 fall (16 credits): INTD 101 First Year Seminar; CRWT 102 Critical Reading and Writing II; General Education Requirement; Quantitative Reasoning—MATH 108, 110 or 121 (MATH 108 highly recommended).
- Year 1 spring (18): General Education Requirement (2); ECON 102 Introduction to Macroeconomics; ACCT 221 Principles of Financial Accounting; PATH 001; BADM 120 Excel Expert Certification Prep* (2).
- Year 2 fall (16): General Education Requirement; INFO 224 Principles of Information Technology; ECON 101 Microeconomics; BADM 225 Management Statistics; PATH 002.
- Year 2 spring (16): General Education Requirement; MKTG 290 Marketing Principles and Practices; ACCT 222 Principles of Managerial Accounting; BADM 223 Business Law I; PATH 003.
- Year 3 fall (16): BADM 301 Ethics in Business*; International Category (ASB Course); MGMT 302 Managing Organizational Behavior; FINC 301 Corporate Finance I.
- Year 3 spring (16): General Education Requirement; MGMT 370 Operations Management; MGMT 340 Human Resource Management; MGMT Elective 1i.
- Year 4 fall (16): MGMT 410 Leadership Strategy and Skill; Free Elective (consider minor, certificate, or second major requirement); MGMT Electives 2i and 3i.
- Year 4 spring (16): BADM 495 Strategic Management; MGMT 475 Management Practicum or MGMT 466 Launchpad: Entrepreneurial Skill Building or MGMT 401 Organizational Analysis; two Free Electives (consider minor, certificate, or second major requirement).
